lead: >-
  Argentina and Ecuador are part of Ada Tours' 32-day itinerary through eight countries. The Argentine section includes walking routes along the Iguazu viewpoints and a visit to Buenos Aires. Between the two countries, travelers cross Bolivia's high-altitude roads in 4×4 vehicles, while in Ecuador they explore Quito and take a boat excursion to the Galapagos Islands. This is a busy journey with mountain roads and changing climates, but no technical mountaineering is advertised.
---

## Adventures on an Argentina + Ecuador itinerary: what's included

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that combine both countries with the "Adventure" interest. Currently, that means a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). **Argentina and Ecuador do not come one after the other:** after Iguazu and Buenos Aires in Argentina, the route continues through Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Ecuador comes on day 21, after a flight from Lima to Quito.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Here, "adventure" primarily means a combination of travel experiences: active walks in natural parks, high-altitude roads across the Altiplano, frequent transfers and boat excursions in the Galapagos. It does not mean that an ascent of Aconcagua is scheduled in Argentina or a summit trek on Cotopaxi in Ecuador. Neither of these independent sporting activities is included in this tour.

| Stage | Type of physical demands |
|---|---|
| Iguazu, Argentina | Walking routes through the park |
| Bolivia en route | Altitude and 4×4 vehicles |
| Quito, Ecuador | A high-altitude city |
| Galapagos | Boats and island trails |

When choosing the trip, bear in mind that the most demanding high-altitude section lies **between the two countries named in this selection**, while the main active experience in Ecuador takes place at sea rather than on a mountain ascent.

## Argentina: a national park without technical trekking

On day 7, travelers visit the Argentine side of the waterfalls near [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Walkways and viewing paths offer different perspectives on the falls. The heat, high humidity, spray and extended walking make this day more physically active than a typical vehicle-based city excursion.

Nevertheless, the Iguazu visit on this itinerary is **a national-park excursion**, not a camping expedition or a multi-day mountain trek. The preceding stage covers the Brazilian side of the falls. A flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) follows, with city sightseeing, an evening of tango and a visit to Uruguay. These days offer some recovery before the high-altitude section, although the pace of travel remains demanding.

If you are specifically looking for Argentine hiking trails, glaciers, challenging climbs or a long route through Patagonia, compare the [adventure tours in Argentina](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/). Iguazu provides a very different experience and calls for different preparation.

## The main altitude challenge between the countries: Atacama and Bolivia

After Buenos Aires, the group flies to Santiago, then to Calama, and travels onward to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A two-day 4×4 route then begins across the Bolivian border. Along the way you will see high-altitude lagoons, geothermal areas, salt flats and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

Some stretches lie **above 4,000 m**. The physical challenge comes from altitude, bumpy off-road travel, long hours sitting in a vehicle, early starts and cold air. No special mountaineering skills are required, but the journey may be tiring even for physically fit travelers.

The sequence of overnight stays, time to acclimatize and avoiding unnecessary exertion after reaching altitude are particularly important. If you have heart or lung conditions, are pregnant or have previously experienced pronounced altitude reactions, discuss the itinerary with a doctor in advance. Opportunities for rapid descent and medical care can be limited in remote areas.

After Bolivia, the itinerary continues through the Lake Titicaca region, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) before reaching Ecuador. The label "Argentina + Ecuador" must therefore not conceal the most demanding section between them: a substantial excursion itinerary in its own right, rather than a simple transfer.

## Ecuador: from high-altitude Quito to Galapagos boat excursions

The Ecuadorian section starts in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The city stands approximately 2,800–2,850 m above sea level, so the altitude change can be noticeable again after arriving from a lowland airport. The day is devoted to the colonial center, city panoramas, [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and the Intiñan Museum. Climbing a volcano is not included that day.

After flying to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), travelers visit Baltra and [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). One day includes a boat excursion **on one of two alternative routes**: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrion. The option is selected when the itinerary is confirmed, so the two must not be combined into one mandatory excursion.

This is a different kind of adventure from the Altiplano: boat motion, disembarking, walking over natural ground and, on the relevant confirmed route, the possibility of swimming or snorkeling. Marine activities depend on the chosen island, sea conditions and the guides' instructions. Snorkeling is not scuba diving and does not imply that equipment-assisted dives are included.

The Galapagos have special conservation rules and visitor-control documentation. Ada Tours helps clarify the island itinerary and procedures planned for your dates, coordinating flights and baggage requirements with the other countries.

## How to assess the itinerary's difficulty before booking

There are **three distinct types of demands** to consider on this journey.

The first is the number of transfers over 32 days. International and domestic flights, road travel and boat transport mean early departures and less free time than a leisurely holiday in one country.

The second is altitude. Buenos Aires and Iguazu are at very different elevations from the Bolivian Altiplano and Quito. Discuss the daily pace, road conditions and opportunities to rest at specific stops with the organizer in advance.

The third is island activity. You should be comfortable boarding a boat, wear suitable closed shoes on rocky terrain, protect yourself from the sun and be prepared for swimming if it is included in the selected option. Travelers with limited mobility need to check the exact landing arrangements beforehand; an island's name alone does not establish accessibility.

If you want mountain hikes **specifically in Ecuador**, explore the [adventure itineraries in Ecuador](/interests/adventure/tours/ecuador/). For a broader geographical overview and a comparison of experiences, see the [Argentina and Ecuador combination without an interest filter](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Argentina–Ecuador adventure tour

### Is climbing Aconcagua or Cotopaxi included?

No. Neither ascent is part of our 32-day journey. The adventurous aspects are the high-altitude drives, nature excursions and a day at sea among the islands.

### Do I need to know how to drive an off-road vehicle in Bolivia?

No. The itinerary describes an organized 4×4 journey with a driver and guide. For participants, the main considerations are tolerance for long drives, altitude and climatic conditions.

### Are all Galapagos island excursions compulsory?

You will take one boat excursion on one of the alternative routes. The conditions and actual island option are confirmed at booking. The itinerary does not promise visits to both North Seymour and South Plaza.

### Can the itinerary be shortened to just two countries?

The existing [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes eight main countries. A journey limited to Argentina and Ecuador would require a different arrangement of flights, active days and budget, to be discussed separately.

lead: >-
  On one extended Ada Tours itinerary, Argentina and Ecuador reveal two distinct cultural worlds of South America. In Buenos Aires, travelers encounter the neighborhoods of an immigrant city and its tango traditions; in Quito, the colonial center, the Quito School of art and the history of the equator. Between these destinations the journey crosses Chile, Bolivia and Peru, visiting monuments of pre-Inca and Inca civilizations. This is a cultural itinerary across eight countries, not a short flight between two capitals.
---

## From tango to the Quito School: the cultural idea behind the journey

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring both Argentina and Ecuador on the main itinerary and substantial cultural and historical excursions. We offer [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Its cultural stops form a sequence stretching from Atlantic cities to the Andes: [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), Montevideo, Santiago, Tiwanaku, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

**Argentina and Ecuador are separated by several countries and almost two weeks of travel on this tour.** The cultural appeal therefore emerges not from comparing two similar sightseeing tours, but from moving between different historical traditions. Buenos Aires introduces the urban culture of the Río de la Plata basin. Quito reveals the interplay of indigenous Andean traditions and Spanish colonial art. The intervening section adds the archaeological history of highland civilizations.

| Stage | Main theme |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | Immigration and tango |
| Bolivia and Peru | Pre-Inca and Inca heritage |
| Quito | Colonial art |
| Galapagos | Natural history, not a museum tour |

The last row matters: Ecuador also includes the Galapagos, but the island days focus on nature. The "Culture and History" tag does not mean that every day is filled with museums.

## Argentina: historic neighborhoods and living tango

Day 8 features a sightseeing tour of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and an evening tango show with dinner. The tour passes through both old and modern districts. [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/) and San Telmo show the history of Buenos Aires as a multilingual port city especially clearly. [Recoleta](/argentina/place/recoleta/) has a different urban character, with monumental architecture, squares and a historic cemetery. Puerto Madero represents the more contemporary waterfront.

Tango on this journey is **an actual scheduled event**, not merely a decorative mention of Argentine culture. In the evening, you will attend a show with dinner. Yet tango is more than a stage performance: it developed within the urban worlds of Buenos Aires and Montevideo at the meeting point of musical and dance traditions. UNESCO inscribed the shared Argentine-Uruguayan tango tradition on its intangible heritage list in 2009.

The next day connects directly with [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/): travelers take a ferry there and return to Buenos Aires. This Uruguayan stop offers an opportunity to understand the cultural links between the two shores of the Río de la Plata. It also calls for separate attention to border-crossing rules: a single-day excursion does not override Uruguay's immigration requirements.

If you want to explore other Argentine cities, the museums of Córdoba or historic regions outside the capital, compare the [cultural and historical tours in Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/). On the 32-day itinerary, the Argentine section is limited to Iguazu, Buenos Aires and the excursion to Montevideo.

## Between the two countries: Andean history you cannot leave out

After Buenos Aires, the journey continues through Chile, Bolivia and Peru. These countries are essential to the cultural significance of the itinerary. In Bolivia, travelers visit the Tiwanaku archaeological complex. On the way toward Peru, they encounter the traditions of Lake Titicaca and the Uros Islands. The [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) region preserves monuments of the Inca Empire alongside architecture from the later colonial period.

The Peruvian section includes [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), historic buildings in Cusco and a sightseeing tour of Lima. These are substantial excursion days, not technical stopovers. At Machu Picchu, the visiting sequence depends on the specific entry-ticket circuit, time slot and transport schedule. Cutting several days from the trip therefore affects access to the sites, not merely hotel nights.

**The purpose of this extended itinerary is to see both the connections and differences between South America's historical cultures.** Traveling only between Buenos Aires and Quito would be a separate product: Bolivia and Peru, with their major cultural stages, would drop out, while flights and the program would change. The existing price and services of the 32-day tour cannot automatically be applied to such an option.

## Ecuador: colonial Quito and the “Middle of the World”

On day 21, travelers arrive in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The following day includes the historic center and an excursion to the equator. Quito stands at around 2,850 m, so even an ordinary walk along old streets after flying can feel different from walking in Buenos Aires.

Quito's historic center has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1978. Its celebrated artistic school brought together European artistic techniques and the work of local craftspeople. Churches, stone and wood carvings, façades and the arrangement of neighborhoods all matter to understanding the city; simply listing buildings tells less than the story of how they came to be.

You will also visit [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and the [Intiñan Museum](/ecuador/place/intinan-museum/). These sites introduce the history of geodetic measurements, how European expeditions determined the equator's position, and how that story is presented to visitors today. The monument's marked line and the equator's actual position are not the same thing; entertaining demonstrations should not be presented as rigorous scientific methods for determining latitude.

After Quito, the group heads to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The focus there shifts to natural history: marine wildlife, islands and conservation rules. Quito's cultural excursions must not be conflated with the island visit or used to promise museums on every Galapagos day.

## Balancing historical sights with a demanding travel schedule

The journey lasts 32 days, but its cultural experiences extend well beyond calendar days spent "in museums." Flights, high-altitude roads and country changes come between the sights. You need to leave enough energy for walking tours after travel days and know in advance which activities are tied to fixed times: the tango evening, city excursions, the Machu Picchu trip and Quito's architectural sites.

The language of guiding matters for historical excursions. Certain parts of the program have Russian-speaking guides; others have English-speaking guides. Before booking, confirm the guiding arrangements for **each day that interests you**, rather than assuming the entire 32-day trip uses one language.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the order of countries, visits to cultural sites and the time available between them. If you primarily want a more in-depth exploration of Ecuador, compare the [cultural tours in Ecuador](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/). To retain all eight countries and their historical stages, explore the full [multi-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) and its calendar.

## Frequently asked questions about the cultures of Argentina and Ecuador

### Is a tango show in Buenos Aires included?

Yes. The current 32-day itinerary includes an evening tango show with dinner in the Argentine capital. The restaurant and service-format details are specified in the conditions of the particular tour.

### Can I visit Cusco and Machu Picchu between Argentina and Ecuador?

Yes. On this extended tour, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) form part of the Peruvian stage before the flight to Quito. Their actual transport sequence and entry tickets must be taken into account.

### Is the equator part of the Quito visit?

Yes. The sightseeing day mentions [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and [Intiñan](/ecuador/place/intinan-museum/). These belong to the Ecuadorian city program; they are not another country or a trek.

### Is the itinerary suitable for someone interested only in Argentina and Ecuador?

Our [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers eight countries, with Bolivia and Peru in between providing a significant share of the cultural program. A two-country alternative would require separate agreement on its content and cost.

  A journey through Argentina and Ecuador can introduce you to two very different natural areas: Iguazu Falls and the volcanic Galapagos Islands. On the current 32-day tour, several other countries separate these stages. We explain the nature excursions included and the itinerary's actual sequence.
---

## Iguazu and the Galapagos on one journey

In Argentina, nature greets travelers with enormous cascades and humid subtropical forest. The [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador offer a completely different environment: volcanic shores, the ocean and nature excursions across the islands. You can combine these experiences on one extended trip, although many other stops lie between them.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is a [32-day itinerary across eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), not a separate short tour limited to Argentina and Ecuador. The full geography is shown in the [general combination catalog](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador/).

## Argentina: a day in nature at Iguazu

The program includes both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu Falls. On the Argentine side, the route takes in the [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area and its national park. Here, visitors see the cascades and forest from a different direction than at the Brazilian viewpoints.

It is worth distinguishing a nature excursion from wildlife watching. There is tropical forest around the waterfalls, but that does not mean a special animal-watching outing is automatically included. After this nature-focused day, travelers continue to Buenos Aires. The Argentine section thus combines nature and the city rather than several consecutive days at the falls.

For a longer visit to the national park, compare [nature tours in Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) and the number of days their itineraries allocate to Iguazu.

## Ecuador: the Galapagos with alternative routes

After many stops in other countries, you arrive in Quito and continue to the Galapagos. The itinerary includes [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The following day offers two **alternative options**: Seymour and Bachas **or** South Plaza and Cape Carrion.

This distinction is essential. The four places should not all be treated as compulsory stops on one day: the itinerary provides for one of the two options. Before departure, confirm the available route, landing arrangements and associated conditions.

The islands are subject to conservation rules. Sea conditions, access restrictions and the chosen program shape each excursion. An encounter with any particular animal in the wild cannot be guaranteed. For a more detailed exploration of this region, see [nature journeys in Ecuador](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/).

## The central trade-off: geographical breadth or time in nature

Between the Argentine waterfalls and the Ecuadorian islands, travelers visit Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru, as well as historical and urban sights. These are substantial stages of the journey in their own right, involving flights and road transfers. A 32-day duration does not mean 32 days in the national parks of Argentina and Ecuador.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If your main goal is to see the widest variety of South American landscapes, this itinerary provides that diversity. If you would rather explore Iguazu or the island ecosystems in depth, a route covering fewer countries and allowing more time at each destination may be more appealing.

If birds and animals are your primary interest, explore the ["Wildlife and Safari"](/interests/wildlife/) category. In every case, only the wildlife observations and excursions actually specified in the itinerary should be treated as included.

## Preparing for contrasting natural environments

For Iguazu, bring comfortable non-slip footwear and protection against spray. For the Galapagos, you will need sun protection, readiness for boat transfers and respect for protected-area rules. Weather and activity levels affect both experiences, but the ways these places are visited differ.

The eight-country itinerary involves several flights. When choosing it, check connections, the actual time allocated to the waterfalls and islands, and entry and transit requirements for **every** country on the route according to your citizenship.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I see Iguazu and the Galapagos on the same journey?

Yes. Both natural areas feature in the [32-day tour across eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

### Are all the listed island excursions scheduled?

No. The Galapagos day offers alternatives: Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Cape Carrion.

### What nature experiences does Argentina offer on this itinerary?

The principal nature-focused stage is the Argentine side of Iguazu. The other Argentine days also include Buenos Aires.

### Is the whole itinerary focused on nature?

There are important nature stops, but also cities, culture, archaeology and lengthy travel sections.

## What you may see: the Iguazu forest and Galapagos wildlife

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Ecuador on the main route and the "Wildlife and Safari" interest. On this [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), the Argentine side of Iguazu falls on day 7, while the Ecuadorian island days come in the final third of the itinerary. **The two natural areas are separated by several countries and different types of transport.**

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

They are especially interesting to compare because their wildlife habitats are so different. [Argentina's Iguazu region](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) is a subtropical forest of waterfalls, tall tree canopies and land animals of the humid tropics. The [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) are a volcanic archipelago where seabirds, reptiles, coastal wildlife and island isolation define the experience.

| Argentina | Ecuador |
|---|---|
| Forest around waterfalls | Islands and ocean |
| Coatis, toucans, monkeys | Boobies, iguanas, tortoises |
| Walkways and trails | Boats and island landings |

The animals listed are characteristic of their respective areas and appear in conservation information about these places. **This is not a list of species guaranteed to be seen on the tour.** The itinerary specifies excursions and visiting sites, not the behavior of wild animals.

## Iguazu: watching the forest when the main excursion focuses on waterfalls

On the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, you will join a group excursion through the national park. Around [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), part of the Selva Paranaense, or Upper Paraná Atlantic Forest, is protected. Argentina's national parks authority lists coatis, monkeys, toucans, agoutis, brocket deer and many other local animals. For birds, the layered vegetation, forest edges and aquatic habitats are particularly important.

Tourist walkways run through greenery near the waterfalls, but the program does not include a dedicated wildlife photography expedition, a search for jaguars or a separate multi-day birdwatching trip. You may happen to encounter animals while listening carefully and keeping your distance. Even coatis that visitors see frequently must not be fed: they remain wild, however accustomed they may be to people.

Travelers also see the Brazilian side of the falls in the preceding stage. It provides another perspective on the cascades, but **Brazil's Bird Park is only a possible additional activity**, not an obligatory visit. An optional excursion must not be added to the guaranteed contents of a nature tour.

For travelers mainly interested in Argentina's wildlife, there are [other wildlife-watching tours in Argentina](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/), including routes through entirely different regions. Our multi-country journey provides one excursion day at Iguazu, followed by a flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

## Galapagos: different islands, different wildlife encounters

The Ecuadorian stage starts in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), with a city excursion. The group then flies to the archipelago via [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) and stays on [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). You will explore the island and its natural areas and take a boat excursion on one of two routes.

**Route 1: North Seymour and Bachas.** The day focuses on observing colonies of frigatebirds, blue-footed boobies, sea lions and marine iguanas. It then continues toward Bachas Beach. In suitable conditions, shorebirds may be seen there, and the included program allows beach time and snorkeling according to the actual plan for the day.

**Route 2: South Plaza and Cape Carrion.** This is a different island route, with its own coastal and marine wildlife observations. Boat crossings and landings from the two options are not added together: the tour provides **one alternative boat excursion**, with the specific route confirmed when organizing the trip.

Your chance of seeing particular species and the islands you actually visit depend on the route selected. Blue-footed boobies, marine iguanas and frigatebirds are not "scenery" that can be guaranteed at a chosen place and hour. Wildlife photographers should discuss this before the island day's arrangements are finalized.

Beyond the excursion to particular islands, it is useful to distinguish land-based exploration of the Santa Cruz highlands from a boat outing. Accessibility, light, wind, walking time and rules of conduct differ between inland and coastal areas. If the Galapagos are your sole goal, [wildlife itineraries in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) allow you to consider other island or mainland formats instead of the entire 32-day continental journey.

## Why the season alone cannot determine wildlife encounters

The journey takes place during the South American spring. Iguazu is a humid subtropical environment where rain and water levels affect walking comfort and views of the falls. In the Galapagos, climate and sea conditions depend on ocean currents; the islands' weather in October and November need not resemble that of the Argentine forest. Different clothing layers, waterproof protection for equipment and flexibility for changing conditions are necessary.

Several factors determine the nature excursion of the day: island access, boat movements, protected-area restrictions, transport schedules and your own physical readiness. Early hours can be favorable for observations, but they do not guarantee an animal in your photographs. The timing of land and marine activities should be checked against the **actual itinerary**, not an abstract "best month for Ecuador."

The 32-day program also crosses highland areas of Bolivia and Peru between Iguazu and the archipelago. They require their own clothing and altitude considerations. If a participant has limits involving exertion, altitude or seasickness, Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence of stops and check the conditions of specific excursions. A general claim that the journey suits everyone would be no substitute.

## Wildlife protection rules matter more than a close-up photograph

The Galapagos have separate entry procedures, biosecurity controls and rules for visiting protected areas. Visitors cannot simply treat a conservation site as somewhere they may wander freely. Routes and accompanying guides depend on local access rules. Argentina's Iguazu National Park also has regulations and restrictions on interactions with animals.

For photography, choose a moderate focal length, plan how to protect equipment from rain and sea spray, never use food or bait, and follow the guide's instructions. Travelers hoping to spend a very long time photographing a single species should understand that **an excursion group moves according to its itinerary**. A specialized photography tour would need different time at each site and different arrangements.

## Choosing between the full itinerary and a nature trip to only two countries

The extended [Argentina + Ecuador itinerary](/multi-country/argentina_ecuador/) suits travelers interested in seeing natural regions as part of a long journey across South America. Its strength is the contrast between humid forest, the Andes and islands within one trip.

If your aim is to observe particular birds, reptiles or other animals over several days, the full eight-country journey may be too densely scheduled. An individual Iguazu–Galapagos combination can be discussed separately, but **we are not offering a ready-made two-country package here with the same conditions and price**. New flights, a visiting sequence, overnight stays and island arrangements would be needed.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentina's and Ecuador's wildlife

### Can I see coatis at Iguazu?

Coatis live in the national park and visitors may encounter them, but a particular sighting depends on the animals and circumstances. The excursion primarily focuses on the waterfalls, and feeding wildlife is prohibited.

### Can I see frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies in one day?

Such sightings are possible around North Seymour, which features on one of the alternative routes. First, confirm that this particular island day has been selected. Even then, bird behavior and viewing conditions cannot be guaranteed.

### Are both Galapagos boat excursions included?

No. Two alternative options are described: North Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Cape Carrion. The final option is confirmed when organizing the journey.

### Is one day at Iguazu sufficient for specialized birdwatching?

A single excursion day offers a first introduction to the forest, but it cannot replace several days searching for species with a specialist guide. An in-depth birdwatching program needs a different amount of time and different content.

### Can I skip the countries between Argentina and Ecuador and keep Iguazu and the Galapagos?

That combination would require a separately agreed itinerary. The published [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) crosses eight countries, so simply removing days would not preserve the original logistics or price.

## How an Argentina, Peru and Ecuador itinerary works

In [Argentina](/argentina/), the journey may begin with the natural spectacle of Iguazu and city walks in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). [Peru](/peru/) offers a very different route: Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). In [Ecuador](/ecuador/), the Andean cities include [Quito and the Cotopaxi region](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), followed by a truly distinctive island stage: the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all three countries on the main itinerary. The confirmed ready-made program is a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Alongside these three countries, it covers Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Colombia. **A three-country selection does not mean a separate ready-made tour of only these three countries is currently available.** A shorter route can be planned individually, with different dates, flight segments and services.

## From Buenos Aires to the Galapagos: the logic of the actual itinerary

After its Brazilian stage, the 32-day journey takes in the Argentine side of Iguazu and Buenos Aires, followed by Uruguay, Chile and Bolivia. In Peru, travelers reach Lake Titicaca, travel via Cusco to Machu Picchu, visit Lima and **fly from Lima to Quito**. After exploring the Ecuadorian capital and the equator, the Galapagos section begins. The program includes Santa Cruz Island, and one excursion day follows one of two alternative island routes. The Ecuadorian stage ends with arrival in [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/), after which the itinerary continues to Colombia.

That is the actual sequence of the published extended tour. Other countries separate Argentina and Peru, while Peru and Ecuador are connected by air on this route despite sharing a land border. For a shorter journey, crossing the border overland and flying are distinct options: time, road access, altitude and overnight stays must all be compared. You cannot simply remove five countries from the existing 32-day program and retain the same flights or price.

| Stage | What to arrange in advance |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazu, Buenos Aires and onward departure |
| Peru | Cusco's altitude, the train and Machu Picchu entry time |
| Ecuador | Galapagos flights, island permits and excursions |

We help determine the order of cities, connection times, hotels and ground transfers. If the Galapagos and Machu Picchu are the main priorities, these two stages should anchor the calendar: both are subject to restrictions on access, tickets and excursion dates. Stops in Argentina can then be arranged around those dates.

## Travel documents for Russian citizens: three countries and separate island procedures

According to information from the Consular Department of Russia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, checked on **16 October 2026**, citizens of the Russian Federation holding valid ordinary international passports can visit Argentina, Peru and Ecuador visa-free for tourism for **up to 90 days in each 180-day period**, subject to each country's rules. There is no common visa for the three countries; each entry is assessed separately. Travelers of other nationalities or with a non-standard purpose of travel need to check the requirements applicable to them.

Peru's immigration authority officially requires passports to remain valid for at least six months upon entry. Before booking, also check transit arrangements through third countries, proof of onward travel, travel documents for children and baggage rules. On the eight-country tour, documents must be checked for the entire itinerary, including the countries between Argentina and Peru.

**The Galapagos Islands require additional procedures even after lawful entry into Ecuador.** Before an island flight from Quito or Guayaquil, travelers obtain a TCT transit control card and undergo a baggage biosecurity inspection. Upon arrival on the islands, a separate protected-area visitor fee applies. The rate depends on the category of traveler and may differ for adults and children. When preparing the budget, establish whether the TCT and environmental fee are included in the particular offer; their inclusion cannot be assumed merely because flights to the islands are provided.

## Machu Picchu and the Galapagos: two independent scheduling constraints

To visit [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), you must select a date, an available entry time and an authorized visitor circuit. Peru's Ministry of Culture sells tickets subject to capacity limits; simply arriving in Cusco does not guarantee entry on any desired date. On the existing 32-day tour, train tickets to Machu Picchu and the specified entrance tickets are listed as included services, but the actual circuit and conditions are confirmed when arranging the journey.

The Galapagos present other considerations: domestic flights, checks on items brought onto the islands, permitted visiting sites and weather for boat trips. The current program **includes one of two alternatives**: North Seymour with Bachas Beach, or South Plaza with Cape Carrion. Both options are not promised together. The choice is confirmed after booking, so when comparing itineraries, ask which specific island day is available on your travel dates.

For travelers who particularly want to visit a specific island or see a certain animal species, this distinction matters more than the general phrase "Galapagos tour." The islands have seasonal variations in wildlife observation, sea conditions and underwater visibility. A realistic plan specifies the available excursion rather than promising an encounter with a particular animal.

## Climate and altitude: why varied clothing and acclimatization time matter

October and November are spring in the Southern Hemisphere in Buenos Aires. In the Peruvian Andes, cool nights and intense sunshine coincide with high altitude. [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) stands at approximately 3,350 m above sea level, while the [Puno and Titicaca region](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) is even higher. Quito is high in the equatorial Andes, whereas the Galapagos are at sea level. Temperatures and physical demands change several times during a single trip.

Pack light clothing for warm cities and islands, a warm mid-layer for high elevations, wind- and rainproof outerwear, shoes suited to stone steps and urban walks, and sun protection. Match your baggage to the actual allowances of each domestic airline. Before island excursions, discuss boat boarding, motion sickness and sea conditions.

**Rapid ascent to high altitude can cause altitude sickness even in physically fit people.** Limit exertion during the first high-altitude stages and discuss individual risks with a doctor, especially if you have heart or lung conditions. Travel insurance should cover the listed countries, mountain sections and relevant activities. Medical requirements for vaccinations and disease prevention depend on specific regions and previous transit, so final advice must be checked against the complete itinerary rather than just the names of the three countries.

## Money: the Argentine peso, Peruvian sol and US dollar

Transactions in Argentina are denominated in Argentine pesos, in Peru in soles, while in Ecuador **the official currency is the US dollar**. This is a convenient feature of Ecuador, but it does not imply that US-dollar cash can be spent in Argentina or Peru without costs or restrictions.

When setting your budget, break down expenses into flights, accommodation, admission tickets, excursions and payments on location. Separately paid island fees and optional activities have their own pricing arrangements. Check exchange costs and access to cash withdrawals before departure. The published tour has its own list of included and excluded services, which should be read instead of estimating the price solely from the number of countries.

Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards cannot be relied upon for international payments. For a foreign-issued card, check whether it actually works in all three countries, as well as fees and limits. Prepare alternative funds and payment methods before departure. We can help discuss local expenses and payment procedures, but cannot guarantee that a particular bank's card will work or that currency exchange will be available on site.

## How to choose your itinerary and duration

If you want to see as much of South America as possible, the [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) combines both sides of Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Lake Titicaca, Machu Picchu, Quito, the Galapagos and Colombia. According to the published program, accommodation is in 4-star hotels, domestic flights and the specified excursions are included, and the international flight is excluded. It is a packed journey using several forms of transport.

If your principal interests are Inca history and the islands' natural world, compare [tours in Peru](/peru/tour/) and [tours in Ecuador](/ecuador/tour/) first, choose a suitable duration and then add [Argentina](/argentina/tour/) with Buenos Aires or Iguazu. Whether to choose a slower or fuller itinerary depends on time at altitude, ticket availability and your willingness to fly frequently. Other combinations are listed in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a ready-made tour limited to Argentina, Peru and Ecuador?

This selection confirms a ready-made 32-day itinerary through eight countries that includes all three named countries as part of the main program. A separate three-country trip requires agreement on its content and conditions.

### Is entry permission for Ecuador enough to visit the Galapagos?

No. In addition to the usual entry documents, the island stage requires a TCT transit control card, biosecurity inspection and a protected-area visitor fee. Check how those charges are handled under the conditions of the particular tour.

### Must Machu Picchu be booked in advance?

It is best to arrange entry as part of the complete itinerary: official tickets are linked to a date, time and visitor circuit, and capacity is limited. Moving the visit may affect the train journey and subsequent flights.

### Are all Galapagos islands included in the published tour?

No. The program provides one of two alternative island excursions, confirmed after booking. Both options together are not guaranteed.

### How demanding is the journey from Peru to Ecuador?

Cusco and the Lake Titicaca region require attention to altitude acclimatization. The published route then includes a flight from Lima to Quito, followed by the island stage. Physical demands, insurance and the pace of travel should be matched to participants' health and the actual schedule.
